cakkhuloliyā.translation_2: One should abandon, dispel, put an end to, and make non-existent greed for the eyes; one should be desisted, abstinent, and having turned away from greed for the eyes; one should dwell having emerged, escaped, liberated, detached, and disconnected [from it] with a mind that has no limits—this is “with the eyes, one should not be greedy.”

suṃsukābhayaṃ.meaning_2: fear of fierce fish; danger from suṃsuka fish
suṃsukābhayaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of susukābhaya in a list of fears. Part of the compound suṃsukābhayaṃ in the text; accusative singular.
suṃsukābhayaṃ.example_1: Athāparena ākārena bhayaṃ vuccati ajjhattikaṃ cittasamuṭṭhānaṃ bhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso ubbego utrāso, jātibhayaṃ jarābhayaṃ byādhibhayaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ rājabhayaṃ corabhayaṃ aggibhayaṃ udakabhayaṃ attānuvādabhayaṃ parānuvādabhayaṃ daṇḍabhayaṃ duggatibhayaṃ ūmibhayaṃ kumbhīlabhayaṃ āvaṭṭabhayaṃ susukābhayaṃ [suṃsukābhayaṃ (syā.)] ājīvikabhayaṃ asilokabhayaṃ parisāya sārajjabhayaṃ madanabhayaṃ duggatibhayaṃ bhayaṃ bhayānakaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso cetaso ubbego utrāso.
suṃsukābhayaṃ.translation_1: From another angle, fear is described as fear originating in the mind: fear as terror, as trembling, as hair-raising, as mental agitation, as terror, fear of birth, fear of old age, fear of illness, fear of death, fear of kings, fear of bandits, fear of fire, fear of floods, fear of self-reproach, fear of reproach by others, fear of punishment, fear of bad destinations, fear of waves, fear of crocodiles, fear of whirlpools, fear of fierce fish, fear of one’s livelihood, fear of ill-repute, fear of timidity in an assembly, fear of madness, fear of a bad destination, fear as terror, as trembling, as hair-raising, as mental agitation, as terror.

pāribhaṭayayatāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text, in a list of improper ways of obtaining requisites. The form is uncertain; possibly a corruption of pāribhaṭṭhatā or pāribhaṭayatā.
pāribhaṭayayatāya.example_1: Laddhāti laddhā labhitvā adhigantvā vinditvā paṭilabhitvā na kuhanāya, na lapanāya, na nemittikatāya, na nippesikatāya, na lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatāya [nijigiṃsanatāya (sī. syā.)], na kaṭṭhadānena, na veḷudānena, na pattadānena, na pupphadānena, na phaladānena, na sinānadānena, na cuṇṇadānena, na mattikādānena, na dantakaṭṭhadānena, na mukhodakadānena, na cāṭukamyatāya, na muggasūpyatāya [na muggasuppatāya (sī.), na muggasūpatāya (syā.)], na pāribhaṭayayatāya, na pīṭhamaddikatāya [piṭṭhimaṃsikatāya (sī.), piṭṭhimaddikatāya (ka.)], na vatthuvijjāya, na tiracchānavijjāya, na aṅgavijjāya, na nakkhattavijjāya, na dūtagamanena, na pahiṇagamanena, na jaṅghapesaniyena, na vejjakammena, na navakammena, na piṇḍapaṭipiṇḍakena, na dānānuppadānena dhammena samena laddhā labhitvā adhigantvā vinditvā paṭilabhitvāti – laddhā.
pāribhaṭayayatāya.translation_1: Having obtained means having received, attained, experienced, [and] acquired in accordance with the law; not by deceit, not by wheedling, not by hint, not by belittling, not by seeking gain through gain, not by giving wood, not by giving bamboo, not by giving leaves, not by giving flowers, not by giving fruit, not by giving bath-powder, not by giving powder, not by giving clay, not by giving tooth-sticks, not by giving face-washing water, not by fawning, not by mung-bean soup behavior, not by fawning behavior, not by stool-cushion behavior, not by astrology, not by animal-knowledge, not by body-knowledge, not by constellation-knowledge, not by acting as a messenger, not by the going of one who is sent, not by running errands, not by the work of a physician, not by new construction, not by giving alms in return, not by giving back gifts — having obtained, attained, experienced, [and] acquired in accordance with the law — this is 'having obtained'.

pādaloliyena.meaning_2: restlessness of feet; footlooseness; wandering about
pādaloliyena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun formed from pādalola. In the text it appears in the instrumental singular: 'pādaloliyena samannāgato hoti' = 'possessed of footlooseness'. Some analyses may treat it as adj agreeing with bhikkhu, but the neuter abstract noun fits best.
pādaloliyena.example_1: idhekacco bhikkhu pādalolo pādaloliyena samannāgato hoti—
pādaloliyena.example_2: atha vā bhikkhu antosaṅghārāme pādalolo pādaloliyena samannāgato hoti, na atthahetu na kāraṇahetu uddhato avūpasantacitto pariveṇato pariveṇaṃ gacchati, vihārato vihāraṃ gacchati, aḍḍhayogato aḍḍhayogaṃ gacchati, pāsādato pāsādaṃ gacchati, hammiyato hammiyaṃ gacchati, guhato guhaṃ gacchati, leṇato leṇaṃ gacchati, kuṭiyā kuṭiṃ gacchati, kūṭāgārato kūṭāgāraṃ gacchati, aṭṭato aṭṭaṃ gacchati, māḷato māḷaṃ gacchati, uddaṇḍato uddaṇḍaṃ gacchati, upaṭṭhānasālato upaṭṭhānasālaṃ gacchati, maṇḍapato maṇḍapaṃ gacchati, rukkhamūlato rukkhamūlaṃ gacchati, yattha vā pana bhikkhū nisīdanti vā gacchanti vā, tattha ekassa vā dutiyo hoti, dvinnaṃ vā tatiyo hoti, tiṇṇaṃ vā catuttho hoti.

pādaloliyaṃ.meaning_2: restlessness of the feet; fidgeting with the feet; foot-restlessness
pādaloliyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Abstract noun from pādalola (unstable on the feet). Accusative singular in the text, object of pajaheyya. Also occurs in the ablative pādaloliyā.
pādaloliyaṃ.example_1: pādaloliyaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, pādaloliyā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyya careyya vicareyya iriyeyya vatteyya pāleyya yapeyya yāpeyya, paṭisallānārāmo assa paṭisallānarato ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ jhāyī jhānarato ekattamanuyutto paramatthagarukoti—

pādaloliyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] pāda + lola + suffix ṇiya (see PEU), hence nt abstract noun. dhurasampaggaho.meaning_2: grasping the yoke; undertaking the burden; taking up the task
dhurasampaggaho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text part of a list of terms for effort (vīriya), nominative singular. Likely a compound of dhura (yoke; burden) + sampaggaha (grasping, taking up).

parikeḷanā.meaning_2: play; amusement; dalliance; fondness for adornment
parikeḷanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa list of a monastic's vain adornments, following keḷanā; the variant gedhitatā/gedhitattaṃ appears in some editions. Nominative singular in the text.

bhijjheyyuṃ.meaning_2: be broken up; be split; be divided; break apart

bhijjheyyuṃ.example_1: kathaṃ ime nānā assu vinā assu vaggā assu dvidhā assu dvejjhā assu dve pakkhā assu bhijjheyyuṃ na samāgaccheyyuṃ dukkhaṃ na phāsu vihareyyunti.
bhijjheyyuṃ.example_2: Kathaṃ ime nānā assu vinā assu vaggā assu dvedhā assu dvejjhā assu dve pakkhā assu bhijjheyyuṃ na samāgaccheyyuṃ dukkhaṃ na phāsu vihareyyunti.
bhijjheyyuṃ.translation_2: Thinking: “How might these people be separated, be without, be divided, become two-fold, become dual, become two factions, be broken up, not come together, and live in discomfort and unease?”

unnahanā.meaning_2: binding up; tying up; entangling (in flattery); encompassing

unnahanā.example_1: lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa āmisacakkhukassa lokadhammagarukassa yā paresaṃ ālapanā lapanā sallapanā ullapanā samullapanā unnahanā samunnahanā ukkācanā samukkācanā anupiyabhāṇitā cāṭukamyatā muggasūpyatā pāribhaṭyatā parapiṭṭhimaṃsikatā, yā tattha saṇhavācatā sakhilavācatā sithilavācatā apharusavācatā—
unnahanā.example_2: Lābhasakkārasilokasannissitassa pāpicchassa icchāpakatassa āmisacakkhukassa lokadhammagarukassa yā paresaṃ ālapanā lapanā sallapanā ullapanā samullapanā unnahanā samunnahanā ukkācanā samukkācanā [ukkāpanā samukkāpanā (syā.)] anupiyabhāṇitā cātukamyatā muggasūpyatā pāribhaṭayatā parapiṭṭhimaṃsikatā [piṭṭhimaṃsikatā (ka.) visuddhimagge sīlaniddesavaṇṇanā oloketabbā], yā tattha saṇhavācatā sakhilavācatā sithilavācatā [mettavācakatā (syā.)] apharusavācatā – ayaṃ vuccati lapanā.
unnahanā.translation_2: For a person with evil desires, who is characterized by desire, greedy for gains, regarding worldly phenomena as significant, and linked to gain, honor, and fame, whatever addressing of others, flattery, chatting, lifting up, lifting up completely, tying up, binding completely, illuminating, illuminating completely, speaking pleasing words, servility, fawning, cringing, or backbiting, along with whatever gentle speech, moderate speech, soft speech, or sweet speech is there—this is called flattery.

ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā.meaning_2: attainment of the sphere of infinite space; the base of infinite space attainment
ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text has ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā, a variant spelling of ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā (instrumental singular). First of the four immaterial attainments.
ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā.example_1: Idhekacco na uccā kulā pabbajito samāno uccā kulā pabbajitena saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na mahābhogakulā pabbajito samāno mahābhogakulā pabbajitena saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na uḷārabhogakulā pabbajito samāno uḷārabhogakulā pabbajitena saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na suttantiko samāno suttantikena saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na vinayadharo samāno vinayadharena … na dhammakathiko samāno dhammakathikena … na āraññiko samāno āraññakena … na piṇḍapātiko samāno piṇḍapātikena … na paṃsukūliko samāno paṃsukūlikena … na tecīvariko samāno tecīvarakena … na sapadānacāriko samāno sapadānacārikena … na khalupacchābhattiko samāno khalupacchābhattikena … na nesajjiko samāno nesaññikena … na yathāsanthatiko samāno yathāsanthatikena saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhī samāno paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhinā saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena, na dutiyassa jhānassa lābhī samāno dutiyassa … na tatiyassa jhānassa lābhī samāno tatiyassa … na catutthassa jhānassa lābhī samāno lābhī samāno catutthassa … na ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā lābhī samāno ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā … na viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā lābhī samāno viññāṇañcāyatana samāpattiyā … na ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā lābhī samāno ākiñcaññāyatana samāpattiyā … na nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā lābhī samāno nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā lābhinā saddhiṃ sadisaṃ attānaṃ karoti cittena – idaṃ cetasikaṃ pāgabbhiyaṃ.
ākāsanañcāyatanasamāpattiyā.translation_1: Here, someone, although not gone forth from a high-status family, makes himself equal in mind to one who has gone forth from a high-status family; although not gone forth from a family of great wealth, he makes himself equal in mind to one who has gone forth from a family of great wealth; although not gone forth from a family of eminent wealth, he makes himself equal in mind to one who has gone forth from a family of eminent wealth; although not a reciter of the Suttas, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a reciter of the Suttas; although not an expert on the discipline, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is an expert on the discipline; although not a speaker on the Dhamma, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a speaker on the Dhamma; although not a forest dweller, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a forest dweller; although not an eater of almsfood, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is an eater of almsfood; although not a wearer of rag-robes, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a wearer of rag-robes; although not a wearer of the triple robe, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a wearer of the triple robe; although not a continuous alms-walker, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a continuous alms-walker; although not one who does not eat in the evening, he makes himself equal in mind to one who does not eat in the evening; although not a continuous sitter, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a continuous sitter; although not an any-bed user, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is an any-bed user; although not a recipient of the first jhāna, he makes himself equal in mind to one who is a recipient of the first jhāna; [similarly for the other jhānas and immaterial attainments]—this is mental presumption.

parisaṭho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Intensive compound of saṭha; nominative singular in the text, describing a deceitful person.
parisaṭho.example_1: idhekacco saṭho hoti parisaṭho, yaṃ tattha saṭhaṃ saṭhatā sāṭheyyaṃ kakkaratā kakkariyaṃ parikkhattatā pārikkhattiyaṃ—
parisaṭho.example_2: Idhekacco saṭho hoti parisaṭho, yaṃ tattha saṭhaṃ saṭhatā sāṭheyyaṃ kakkaratā kakkariyaṃ parikkhattatā pārikkhattiyaṃ – idaṃ vuccati sāṭheyyaṃ.
parisaṭho.translation_2: Here, someone is deceitful and is deceitful in every respect; that which is in that individual—the deceit, the state of being deceitful, fraud, the harsh nature, the praiseful state, the entrenched, firm deception—this is called fraud.

khuṃsito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used as an adjective meaning 'insulted, reviled'. The root √khuṃs (insult) is rare; the PEU suggests khusi+ta. In the text it appears in a list of synonyms (dūsito, ghaṭṭito, vambhito, garahito, upavadito) describing one who is insulted or abused.
khuṃsito.example_1: rusitoti dūsito khuṃsito ghaṭṭito vambhito garahito upavadito.
khuṃsito.example_2: dūsito khuṃsito vambhito ghaṭṭito garahito upavadito pharusena kakkhaḷena nappaṭivajjā nappaṭibhaṇeyya, akkosantaṃ na paccakkoseyya, rosantaṃ nappaṭiroseyya, bhaṇḍantaṃ na paṭibhaṇḍeyya, na kalahaṃ kareyya, na bhaṇḍanaṃ kareyya, na viggahaṃ kareyya, na vivādaṃ kareyya, na medhagaṃ kareyya, kalahaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ viggahaṃ vivādaṃ medhagaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, kalahabhaṇḍanaviggahavivādamedhagā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyyāti—

sakkhidhammamanītihamaddasīti.meaning_2: saw the state of a witness, free from led-astray views; saw the truth as a witness, not led astray
sakkhidhammamanītihamaddasīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sakkhidhamma + anītihaṃ + addasī + iti (or similar); a poetic/commentarial description of the Buddha seeing the truth; final -ti is the quotation particle.

napī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + pi, used for emphasis: 'not even, nor'. In the text: 'na bhasmā hoti napī masi' = 'there is no ash, nor even soot'. Sometimes written na pi.
napī.example_2: Passa kammānaṃ daḷhattaṃ, na bhasmā hoti napī masi.
napī.translation_2: See the firmness of their deeds, there is no ash, nor even soot.

disampi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular of disā. In the text it is followed by the sandhi -pi (disampi).
disampi.example_1: ‘‘ Yaṃ yaṃ disaṃ padhāvanti [disampi dhāvanti (syā.)], taṃ taṃ dvāraṃ pidhīyati [pithīyati (sī. syā.)];
disampi.translation_1: “To whatever direction they run, that door is closed;

āvīsīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form āvīsīti in the text is likely āvisi + iti, with the aorist āvisi, but the passage also cites āvisati. Commentarial gloss on āvisi.
āvīsīti.example_1: Disvāti disvā passitvā tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā bhayaṃ pīḷanaṃ ghaṭṭanaṃ upaddavo upasaggo āvisīti [āvīsīti (sī.), āvisatīti (syā.)]– disvā maṃ bhayamāvisi.
āvīsīti.translation_1: “Seeing” means having seen, having perceived, having calculated, having judged, having clarified, having made evident—fear, oppression, agitation, danger, or misfortune entered (me)—thus: “Seeing, fear entered me.”

uppāṭayitvā.meaning_2: having pulled out; having torn out; having uprooted; having eradicated
uppāṭayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive, part of a series of synonyms (uddharitvā, samuddharitvā, pajahitvā) for eradicating a defilement. Sometimes analysed with √paṭh (paṭh + *aya), but √paṭ 1 is preferred here.
uppāṭayitvā.example_1: attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhaccāti attānudiṭṭhiṃ ūhacca samūhacca uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantīkaritvā anabhāvaṃ gametvāti—
uppāṭayitvā.example_2: tameva rāgasallaṃ dosasallaṃ mohasallaṃ mānasallaṃ diṭṭhisallaṃ sokasallaṃ kathaṅkathāsallaṃ abbuyha abbuhitvā uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā pajahitvā vinodetvā byantiṃ karitvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā neva puratthimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na pacchimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na uttaraṃ disaṃ dhāvati na dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ dhāvati.

uppādayitvā.meaning_2: having caused to arise; having produced; having stirred up
uppādayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in a list of absolutives describing the removal of the dart (salla). Causes the arising (of something). Some editions read samuppādayitvā.
uppādayitvā.example_1: Tameva rāgasallaṃ dosasallaṃ mohasallaṃ mānasallaṃ diṭṭhisallaṃ sokasallaṃ kathaṃkathāsallaṃ abbuyha abbuhitvā uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā [uppādayitvā samuppādayitvā (syā. ka.)] pajahitvā vinodetvā byantiṃ karitvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā neva puratthimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na pacchimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na uttaraṃ disaṃ dhāvati na dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ dhāvati.
uppādayitvā.translation_1: Having drawn out, pulled out, removed, completely removed, struck out, completely struck out, abandoned, dispelled, made an end of, and reduced to non-existence that very dart of lust, dart of hatred, dart of delusion, dart of conceit, dart of view, dart of sorrow, and dart of uncertainty and wondering, he does not run east, does not run west, does not run north, does not run south.

samuppādayitvā.meaning_2: having caused to arise; having produced; having generated
samuppādayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for uppādayitvā (digital PDB marks the samuppādayitvā reading as the Siamese/Thai edition). Absolutive in a list of absolutives describing removing the darts of defilement.
samuppādayitvā.example_1: Tameva rāgasallaṃ dosasallaṃ mohasallaṃ mānasallaṃ diṭṭhisallaṃ sokasallaṃ kathaṃkathāsallaṃ abbuyha abbuhitvā uddharitvā samuddharitvā uppāṭayitvā samuppāṭayitvā [uppādayitvā samuppādayitvā (syā. ka.)] pajahitvā vinodetvā byantiṃ karitvā anabhāvaṃ gametvā neva puratthimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na pacchimaṃ disaṃ dhāvati na uttaraṃ disaṃ dhāvati na dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ dhāvati.
samuppādayitvā.translation_1: Having drawn out, pulled out, removed, completely removed, struck out, completely struck out, abandoned, dispelled, made an end of, and reduced to non-existence that very dart of lust, dart of hatred, dart of delusion, dart of conceit, dart of view, dart of sorrow, and dart of uncertainty and wondering, he does not run east, does not run west, does not run north, does not run south.

gīyanti.meaning_2: is sung; is recited; is taken and memorised
gīyanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Passive of gāyati. In the text gīyanti is glossed with niggīyanti, kathīyanti, bhaṇīyanti and, in the second sentence, with gaṇhīyanti uggaṇhīyanti (are taken up and memorised). 3rd plural present passive.
gīyanti.example_1: anugīyantīti gīyanti niggīyanti kathīyanti bhaṇīyanti dīpīyanti voharīyanti.
gīyanti.example_2: atha vā gīyanti gaṇhīyanti uggaṇhīyanti dhārīyanti upadhārīyanti upalakkhīyanti gadhitapaṭilābhāya.

niggīyanti.meaning_2: is sung; is uttered; is spoken; is proclaimed
niggīyanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of anugīyanti in the defining sentence of the Niddesa commentary; passive causative of ni + √gā, meaning 'is sung out; is said'. Present 3rd plural.
niggīyanti.example_1: anugīyantīti gīyanti niggīyanti kathīyanti bhaṇīyanti dīpīyanti voharīyanti.

saṃtiṭṭheyya.meaning_2: should stand firm (in); should remain (in); should persist (in)
saṃtiṭṭheyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular of saṃtiṭṭhati, negated with na in the text: na saṃtiṭṭheyya, 'should not remain in'. Saṃtiṭṭheyya and tiṭṭheyya are used together, both negated with atimāne ('in conceit').
saṃtiṭṭheyya.example_1: Atimāne na tiṭṭheyya na saṃtiṭṭheyya, atimānaṃ pajaheyya vinodeyya byantiṃ kareyya anabhāvaṃ gameyya, atimānā ārato assa virato paṭivirato nikkhanto nissaṭo vippamutto visaññutto vimariyādikatena cetasā vihareyyāti – atimāne na tiṭṭheyya.
saṃtiṭṭheyya.translation_1: One should not remain or stand in conceit; one should abandon, dispel, put an end to, and bring to non-existence conceit; one should be one who has desisted, turned away, abstained, emerged, is freed, is released, is detached, and lives with a mind free of boundaries—that is “one should not remain in conceit.”

paṭivāsetvā.meaning_2: having turned away; having turned back; having withdrawn
paṭivāsetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of paṭivāpetvā; the commentator's gloss takes it as 'having turned away (the mind)'. Absolutive of the causative paṭivāseti.
paṭivāsetvā.example_1: Atha vā sabbasaṅkhāradhātuyā cittaṃ paṭivāpetvā [paṭivāsetvā (ka.)] amatāya dhātuyā cittaṃ upasaṃharati –
paṭivāsetvā.translation_1: Alternatively, having turned the mind away from the element of all volitional formations, one inclines the mind toward the deathless property—

nibbuttiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine i-stem noun; accusative singular in the text. The form is from nibbuti, meaning peace or Nibbāna. PEU also connects it with √vā (to blow) and ni (out).
nibbuttiṃ.example_1: ‘‘ Te nibbuttiṃ āsisamānasā [āsiṃsamānā (sī.), abhimānā (syā.)] dadanti, tanninnacittā [tanninnā tañcittā (ka.)] tadadhimuttā;
nibbuttiṃ.translation_1: “Desiring peace, they give gifts, with minds slanting toward that, and devoted to that;

vuttaṃñhetaṃ.meaning_2: for this is said; for this was said
vuttaṃñhetaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vuttaṃ (past participle of vadati, 'said') + hi (emphatic, 'for; indeed') + etaṃ (pronoun, 'this'). Opening of a quotation; the final -ṃ of vuttaṃ is replaced by ñ before hi.
vuttaṃñhetaṃ.translation_1: This has been said by the Blessed One—

visaritaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular agreeing with taṇhājāliniṃ; visaritaṃ visattikaṃ describes the craving-net as spread out and clinging.
visaritaṃ.example_1: so evaṃ eko adutiyo appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto mahāpadhānaṃ padahanto māraṃ sasenakaṃ namuciṃ kaṇhaṃ pamattabandhuṃ vidhametvā ca taṇhājāliniṃ visaritaṃ visattikaṃ pajahi vinodesi byantīakāsi anabhāvaṅgamesi.
visaritaṃ.example_2: so evaṃ eko adutiyo appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto najjā nerañjarāya tīre bodhirukkhamūle mahāpadhānaṃ padahanto māraṃ sasenaṃ kaṇhaṃ namuciṃ pamattabandhuṃ vidhamitvā taṇhājāliniṃ visaritaṃ visattikaṃ pajahasi vinodesi byantiṃ akāsi anabhāvaṃ gamesi.

sambujjhitabbaṃ.meaning_2: to be fully understood; to be comprehended; to be awakened to
sambujjhitabbaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle used in the Niddesa alongside bujjhitabba, anubujjhitabba, paṭibujjhitabba. Neuter nominative singular in the text.
sambujjhitabbaṃ.example_1: atha vā yaṃ bujjhitabbaṃ anubujjhitabbaṃ paṭibujjhitabbaṃ sambujjhitabbaṃ adhigantabbaṃ phassitabbaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ tena bodhiñāṇena bujjhi anubujjhi paṭibujjhi sambujjhi adhigacchi phassesi sacchākāsi.
sambujjhitabbaṃ.example_2: atha vā yaṃ bujjhitabbaṃ anubujjhitabbaṃ paṭibujjhitabbaṃ sambujjhitabbaṃ adhigantabbaṃ phassitabbaṃ sacchikātabbaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ tena paccekabodhiñāṇena bujjhi anubujjhi paṭibujjhi sambujjhi adhigacchi phassesi sacchākāsīti evaṃ so paccekasambuddho eko anuttaraṃ paccekasambodhiṃ abhisambuddhoti—

ugghātinigghātivītivatto.meaning_2: who has passed beyond vexation and non-vexation; gone beyond agitation and quieting
ugghātinigghātivītivatto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Attributive compound describing one free from attraction and aversion; nominative singular in the text.
ugghātinigghātivītivatto.example_1: ekacce bāhaṃ gandhena limpeyyuṃ, ekacce bāhaṃ vāsiyā taccheyyuṃ, amukasmiṃ natthi rāgo, amukasmiṃ natthi paṭighaṃ, anunayapaṭighavippahīno ugghātinigghātivītivatto anurodhavirodhaṃ samatikkanto.

paṭibāhirā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of paribāhirā in the sentence; nominative plural masculine agreeing with tumhe. Possibly from paṭi + bāhira, 'turned outside, excluded'.
paṭibāhirā.example_1: Sace ahaṃ na paṭiggahessāmi, evaṃ tumhe puññena paribāhirā [paṭibāhirā (ka.)] bhavissatha, na mayhaṃ iminā attho, api ca tumhākaṃyeva anukampāya paṭiggaṇhāmī ’’ ti.
paṭibāhirā.translation_1: If I do not accept, then you will be deprived of merit; I have no need for this, yet I accept it out of compassion for you.’

kivantoti.meaning_2: how much; how great; how many
kivantoti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is kivanto with the quotation particle -ti: kivanto iti. Interrogative adjective meaning 'how much; how many'.

isivātapaṭivātāni.meaning_2: exposed to the winds of the sages; (unaffected by) the winds of the sages?; protected from the winds of the sages
isivātapaṭivātāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Niddesa list of families worthy of resort. The reading and sense are uncertain; the PEU entry suggests isi + vāta + paṭivāta. The context is a stock list, so it is likely a stock positive epithet. Neuter plural in the text.
isivātapaṭivātāni.example_1: yāni vā pana tāni kulāni saddhāni pasannāni opānabhūtāni kāsāvapajjotāni isivātapaṭivātāni atthakāmāni hitakāmāni phāsukāmāni yogakkhemakāmāni bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ, tathārūpāni kulāni sevati bhajati payirupāsati—
isivātapaṭivātāni.example_2: Yāni vā pana tāni kulāni saddhāni pasannāni opānabhūtāni kāsāvapajjotāni isivātapaṭivātāni atthakāmāni hitakāmāni phāsukāmāni yogakkhemakāmāni bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ, tathārūpāni kulāni sevati bhajati payirupāsati – ayampi vuccati gocaro.
isivātapaṭivātāni.translation_2: Whatever those families are that are faithful, serene, acting as a source of support, radiant with the robes, protected by the winds of the sages, desiring what is worthwhile, desiring what is beneficial, desiring what is comfortable, desiring what is safe from the four yokes, toward bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, laymen, and laywomen—he relies on, approaches, and pays homage to such families—this too is called a suitable resort.

paṭibujjhitukāmassa.meaning_2: desiring to awaken (to); wanting to understand; wishing to penetrate
paṭibujjhitukāmassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text, agreeing with the seeker of sambodhi; the -tuṃ infinitive inside the compound is from paṭibujjhati.
paṭibujjhitukāmassa.example_1: taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti—
paṭibujjhitukāmassa.example_2: Taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti – sambodhikāmassa.
paṭibujjhitukāmassa.translation_2: For one who wishes to awaken to that enlightenment, who wishes to know through appropriate practice, who wishes to penetrate it, who wishes to awaken rightly, who wishes to reach it, who wishes to touch it, and who wishes to realize it—that is “for one who desires enlightenment.”

sambujjhitukāmassa.meaning_2: desiring to awaken fully; wishing to attain full enlightenment
sambujjhitukāmassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text, qualifying one who desires sambodhi. Compound of the infinitive sambujjhituṃ and kāma; the form sambujjhitukāmassa is the genitive singular of the compound as a whole.
sambujjhitukāmassa.example_1: taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti—
sambujjhitukāmassa.example_2: Taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti – sambodhikāmassa.
sambujjhitukāmassa.translation_2: For one who wishes to awaken to that enlightenment, who wishes to know through appropriate practice, who wishes to penetrate it, who wishes to awaken rightly, who wishes to reach it, who wishes to touch it, and who wishes to realize it—that is “for one who desires enlightenment.”

phassitukāmassa.meaning_2: wishing to touch; desiring to experience; wanting to contact
phassitukāmassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Desiderative compound with infinitive phassituṃ (from phusati, √phus 1). Genitive singular in the text, qualifying one who wishes to attain sambodhi.
phassitukāmassa.example_1: taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti—
phassitukāmassa.example_2: Taṃ sambodhiṃ bujjhitukāmassa anubujjhitukāmassa paṭibujjhitukāmassa sambujjhitukāmassa adhigantukāmassa phassitukāmassa sacchikātukāmassāti – sambodhikāmassa.
phassitukāmassa.translation_2: For one who wishes to awaken to that enlightenment, who wishes to know through appropriate practice, who wishes to penetrate it, who wishes to awaken rightly, who wishes to reach it, who wishes to touch it, and who wishes to realize it—that is “for one who desires enlightenment.”

madditabbāni.meaning_2: to be crushed; to be trampled; to be destroyed
madditabbāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter nominative plural in -āni, agreeing with the preceding gerundives. Part of a list of things to be overcome and crushed.
madditabbāni.example_1: athāparānipi atthi abhisambhotabbāni abhibhavitabbāni ajjhottharitabbāni pariyādiyitabbāni madditabbāni.

abhisambhavैyyāti.meaning_2: could overcome; would be able to endure
abhisambhavैyyāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written abhisambhavaiyyāti, an alternative optative spelling of abhisambhaveyya with quotative ti. From abhisambhavati, optative 3rd singular. No sentences were found; optative form assumed.

visaṅghacārino.meaning_2: not moving in herds; wandering alone; not gregarious
visaṅghacārino.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (syā.) of asaṅghacārino; nominative plural in the text, agreeing with bhikkhavo. Also resolvable as vi + saṅghacārī.
visaṅghacārino.example_1: Migā viya asaṅghacārino [māgadhā visaṅghacārino (syā.)], aniketā viharanti bhikkhavo.
visaṅghacārino.translation_1: “Like animals, they are non-obstructive wanderers; the bhikkhus dwell without abode.”

cātukamyatāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text, listed among wrong ways of obtaining requisites. The word is an abstract noun from cātukamma, itself a compound of cātu and kamma.
cātukamyatāya.example_1: Cīvaraṃ labhitvā piṇḍapātaṃ labhitvā na kuhanāya, na lapanāya, na nemittikatāya, na nippesikatāya, na lābhena lābhaṃ nijigīsanatāya, na dārudānena, na veḷudānena, na pattadānena, na pupphadānena, na phaladānena, na sinānadānena, na cuṇṇadānena, na mattikādānena, na dantakaṭṭhadānena, na mukhodakadānena, na cātukamyatāya, na muggasūpyatāya, na pāribhaṭyatāya, na pīṭhamaddikatāya, na vatthuvijjāya, na tiracchānavijjāya, na aṅgavijjāya, na nakkhattavijjāya, na dūtagamanena, na pahiṇagamanena, na jaṅghapesanikena, na vejjakammena, na piṇḍapaṭipiṇḍakena, na dānānuppadānena dhammena samena laddhā labhitvā adhigantvā vinditvā paṭilabhitvāti – annañca laddhā vasanañca kāle.
cātukamyatāya.translation_1: Having received a robe, having received almsfood, not for the sake of flattery, not for the sake of deception, not for the sake of omens, not for the sake of hints, not for the sake of seeking gain with gain, not by giving wood, not by giving bamboo, not by giving leaves, not by giving flowers, not by giving fruits, not by giving water for bathing, not by giving powders, not by giving clay, not by giving tooth-sticks, not by giving water for the face, not for the sake of flattery, not for the sake of curry, not for the sake of gossip, not for the sake of supporting others, not by astrology, not by base arts, not by interpreting bodily marks, not by auspicious signs, not by acting as an emissary, not by going on errands, not by serving as a messenger, not by practicing medicine, not by returning alms for alms, not by giving gifts in return for gifts—having obtained them lawfully and righteously, having received them, having reached them, having found them, having acquired them—that is “having received almsfood and clothing in season.”

paṭivinoditvā.meaning_2: having driven away; having dispelled; having removed
paṭivinoditvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of vippajahitvā in these verses; the absolutive of paṭivinodeti, formed from the past participle stem paṭivinodita. No simplex paṭivinodati is attested.
paṭivinoditvā.example_1: Etaṃ rajaṃ vippajahitvā [paṭivinoditvā (ka.)] paṇḍitā, viharanti te vigatarajassa sāsane.
paṭivinoditvā.translation_1: having abandoned this dust, the wise dwell in the Dispensation of the dustless one.
paṭivinoditvā.example_2: Etaṃ rajaṃ vippajahitvā [paṭivinoditvā (ka.) mahāni.209] cakkhumā, tasmā jino vigatarajoti vuccati.
paṭivinoditvā.translation_2: Since the Clear-eyed One has abandoned this corruption, the Victorious Buddha is called ‘one whose corruption has faded away.’

taṇhāgaddūlaṃ.meaning_2: net of craving; snare of craving
taṇhāgaddūlaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, in a list of synonyms for craving. PEU gives both masculine and neuter; the Pāḷi form with -aṃ is ambiguous. gaddūla is usually 'creeper, creeper-net'; the PEU gloss 'bondage' is doubtful.
taṇhāgaddūlaṃ.example_1: yo rāgo sārāgo anunayo anurodho nandī nandirāgo, cittassa sārāgo icchā mucchā ajjhosānaṃ gedho paligedho saṅgo paṅko, ejā māyā janikā sañjananī sibbinī jālinī saritā visattikā, suttaṃ visatā āyūhinī dutiyā paṇidhi bhavanetti, vanaṃ vanatho sandhavo sneho apekkhā paṭibandhu, āsā āsīsanā āsīsitattaṃ, rūpāsā saddāsā gandhāsā rasāsā phoṭṭhabbāsā, lābhāsā dhanāsā puttāsā jīvitāsā, jappā pajappā abhijappā jappanā jappitattaṃ loluppaṃ loluppāyanā loluppāyitattaṃ pucchañjikatā sādhukamyatā, adhammarāgo visamalobho nikanti nikāmanā patthanā pihanā sampatthanā, kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā vibhavataṇhā, rūpataṇhā arūpataṇhā nirodhataṇhā, rūpataṇhā saddataṇhā gandhataṇhā rasataṇhā phoṭṭhabbataṇhā dhammataṇhā, ogho yogo gantho upādānaṃ āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ chadanaṃ bandhanaṃ, upakkileso anusayo pariyuṭṭhānaṃ latā vevicchaṃ, dukkhamūlaṃ dukkhanidānaṃ dukkhappabhavo mārapāso mārabaḷisaṃ māravisayo, taṇhānadī taṇhājālaṃ taṇhāgaddūlaṃ taṇhāsamuddo abhijjhā lobho akusalamūlaṃ.

paṭisaṃyojeyya.meaning_2: could connect; could engage; could join (with)
paṭisaṃyojeyya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular in the text, in a series with paṭibaleyya, kareyya. Denotes ability or possibility: 'could he engage in debate with whom?'.
paṭisaṃyojeyya.example_1: so kena mānena, kāya diṭṭhiyā, kena vā puggalena vādaṃ paṭisaṃyojeyya paṭibaleyya kalahaṃ kareyya bhaṇḍanaṃ kareyya viggahaṃ kareyya vivādaṃ kareyya medhagaṃ kareyya—

taccariko.meaning_2: devoted to that; practising that; intent on that
taccariko.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it describes one whose conduct is bent on that (paññā). bahubbīhi formed with a pronoun (tad).
taccariko.example_1: paññaṃ purakkhatvāti idhekacco paññaṃ purato katvā carati paññādhajo paññāketu paññādhipateyyo vicayabahulo pavicayabahulo pekkhāyanabahulo sampekkhāyanabahulo vibhūtavihārī taccariko tabbahulo taggaruko tanninno tappoṇo tappabbhāro tadadhimutto tadadhipateyyoti.
